verdicts.originalText: Charged Attack frames are for the standard Hydro Charged Attack. When Columbina holds at least 1 Verdant Dew (a resource gained by the party triggering Lunar-Bloom, i.e. Moonridge Dew), her Charged Attack is replaced by Moondew Cleanse — a stamina-free 3-hit AoE Lunar-Bloom (Dendro) attack scaling on her Max HP. Because Verdant Dew depends on team reactions the planner cannot simulate, only the base Charged Attack is shown.
verdicts.proposedText: Shown as the base Hydro Charged Attack. With at least 1 Verdant Dew it becomes a stamina-free 3-hit AoE Dendro (Lunar-Bloom) attack; not modeled, since Verdant Dew comes from team Lunar-Bloom reactions.
verdicts.rationale: Genuine divergence: the Charged Attack shown is the base Hydro one, but at 1+ Verdant Dew it is fully replaced by a stamina-free Dendro Lunar-Bloom attack that is not modeled because Verdant Dew comes from unsimulated team reactions. Compressed to two sentences, dropped this character's/ability's names and the Moondew Cleanse label per the panel-context rule.

verdicts.originalText: The skill's own AoE Hydro DMG on cast (30.1% Max HP @T10) is represented by the frame timing, not as a separate effect. Gravity Ripple follows the on-field character and ticks Hydro DMG. Gravity Interference is off-field DMG that fires only when Columbina's Gravity fills to its limit from party Lunar reactions (~every 6s of continuous Lunar reactions); only the single dominant Lunar reaction type's hit is dealt, so the three variants shown never all fire at once.
verdicts.proposedText: The three off-field Gravity Interference hits fire only when Gravity fills from party Lunar reactions (about every 6s), and only the one matching the dominant reaction lands — never all three at once. This timing is not modeled.
verdicts.rationale: The trust-repair core is that the timeline shows three off-field Gravity Interference variants but only one fires per trigger, on a reaction-driven cadence that is not simulated. The on-cast Hydro representation and the Gravity Ripple summon describe correct tool behavior and were dropped as working behavior.

verdicts.originalText: Moonlit Melancholy transforms the terrain into a stationary Lunar Domain for 20s. Party members inside the domain deal more Lunar Reaction DMG — modeled here as +40% to each Lunar reaction (Lunar-Charged / Lunar-Bloom / Lunar-Crystallize) @T10. In-game this is a Lunar Reaction DMG Bonus (a reaction-multiplier bonus); the planner has no dedicated reaction-bonus stat, so it is shown on the three Lunar DMG Bonus lines. The buff only applies while the active character stands within the domain. The burst's on-cast AoE Hydro DMG (58.0% Max HP @T10) is represented by frame timing, not a separate effect.
verdicts.proposedText: Shown as +40% on the three Lunar-reaction DMG-bonus lines; in game it's one Lunar Reaction DMG Bonus, with no dedicated stat. It applies only while the active character stays in the domain, though shown for the full window.
verdicts.rationale: Two real divergences kept: the single reaction bonus is approximated across three DMG-bonus lines (no dedicated reaction-bonus stat), and its positional requirement (active character inside the domain) is rendered as a full-duration buff. The domain/20s framing and the on-cast Hydro representation are modeled correctly and were dropped as working behavior.

verdicts.originalText: Self-only CRIT Rate. Stacks each time Gravity Interference triggers; because that timing depends on party Lunar reactions the planner cannot simulate, it is shown as a manual buff (up to 3 stacks = +15% CRIT Rate).
verdicts.proposedText: Self-only, not a team buff — it stacks whenever Gravity Interference fires, so it's added manually (up to 3 stacks, +15% CRIT Rate). That cadence depends on party Lunar reactions, which aren't modeled.
verdicts.rationale: Correct content, but rewritten for timeline voice and to avoid the discouraged 'the planner cannot' framing. Preserves scope (self, mirroring the effect's self target), the manual-trigger reason, and the stack/value figures.

verdicts.originalText: The Rainsea Shield (12% of Columbina's Max HP, absorbs Hydro DMG with 250% effectiveness for 8s), the 6 Energy to the active character, and the interruption resistance are mutually exclusive Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam rewards — only ONE fires per Gravity Interference, chosen by the dominant Lunar reaction (Lunar-Crystallize / Lunar-Charged / Lunar-Bloom respectively) and only when the party's Moonsign is Ascendant Gleam. C1 also makes casting Eternal Tides immediately trigger a Gravity Interference (once every 15s).
verdicts.proposedText: The shield, 6 Energy, and interruption resistance all appear, but only one fires per Gravity Interference — chosen by the dominant Lunar reaction, and that timing isn't modeled.
verdicts.rationale: Core divergence: the timeline shows all three rewards together, but only one fires per Gravity Interference by dominant reaction, on an unsimulated cadence. The Moonsign gate is already modeled via the team-faction condition (working behavior); shield parameters and the reward-to-reaction mapping are curator detail; the C1-on-skill retrigger is kit mechanics.

verdicts.originalText: When Gravity Interference triggers, Columbina gains Lunar Brilliance (+40% Max HP, 8s). Under Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam this also converts a share of her Max HP into a stat for the active character — ATK (1% of Max HP), Elemental Mastery (0.35% of Max HP), or DEF (1% of Max HP), chosen by the dominant Lunar reaction, only one at a time. The +34% Gravity accumulation rate makes Gravity Interference fire more often but is not otherwise modeled.
verdicts.proposedText: The +40% Max HP fires with every Gravity Interference; the ATK, EM, and DEF conversions (each a share of Max HP) are mutually exclusive — only the one matching the dominant reaction lands. That timing and the +34% Gravity rate aren't modeled.
verdicts.rationale: The timeline shows the +40% Max HP self buff plus all three active-character stat conversions, but only one conversion fires per trigger by dominant reaction, on an unsimulated cadence; the +34% Gravity rate is also unmodeled. The buff name, exact conversion percentages, 8s duration, and Moonsign gate are modeled or curator detail.

verdicts.originalText: When Gravity Interference triggers, Columbina restores 4 of her own Energy, and the fired Gravity Interference hit gains bonus DMG equal to 12.5% (Lunar-Charged) / 2.5% (Lunar-Bloom) / 12.5% (Lunar-Crystallize) of her Max HP, at most once every 15s. Both scale off her Max HP and are folded into the Gravity Interference hit rather than shown separately.
verdicts.proposedText: Not modeled: the 4 Energy she regains on each Gravity Interference, and the bonus DMG added to that hit (12.5% / 2.5% / 12.5% of Max HP, by dominant Lunar reaction, once per 15s). Both fold into the Gravity Interference hit and aren't shown.
verdicts.rationale: Neither the self-energy nor the reaction-conditional flat DMG is modeled (self-only unsimulated timing / a Max-HP flat add on an unmodelable-cadence hit); the caveat's job is to flag both omissions. Dropped the per-reaction value labels and the imprecise 'both scale off Max HP' (the 4 Energy is a flat grant).

verdicts.originalText: Requires the Lunar Domain (Burst) to be active. When a party member triggers a Lunar reaction inside it, all party members gain +80% CRIT DMG for 8s — but ONLY on damage of the elements involved in that reaction (e.g. a Lunar-Charged reaction buffs Electro and Hydro CRIT DMG). The planner shows a single generic +80% CRIT DMG bar; treat it as element-restricted.
verdicts.proposedText: Shown as one generic +80% CRIT DMG bar, but in game it covers only the elements in the triggering Lunar reaction — a Lunar-Charged reaction buffs Electro and Hydro. It also needs the burst's Lunar Domain active and a Lunar reaction inside it, which isn't modeled.
verdicts.rationale: Key divergence kept: the +80% CRIT DMG bar reads as blanket, but in game it is element-restricted to the triggering reaction, and its dependency on an active Lunar Domain plus an in-domain Lunar reaction is not tracked. The 8s duration and team scope are modeled/shown correctly.
